Origin: scheduled dispatch Routine firing, 2026-09-18T08:14Z (run `2026-09-18T081427-dispatch-standalone`, group run `2026-09-18T082615-record-1739-2336`)

Defer-reason: tangential — found while dispatching #1739/#2336 to a successful merge (PR #2596); the dispatch task itself completed correctly (the dispatching session closed the gap manually), this is a follow-up on the template defect observed along the way.

## Current State

`plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s second-call template (review,polish,wrap-up) contains two directly contradictory instructions about who archives the run directory when `OUTCOME: merged`:

- The "Working directory" paragraph states, unconditionally: "Worktree removal and run-dir archival are the dispatching session's responsibility, not yours — do NOT call `ExitWorktree` or `git worktree remove`, and do NOT archive the run directory yourself, **on any outcome (merged, armed, pending-review, ready-to-merge, failed, or blocked)**."
- The `integration-model: pr-first` outcome-vocabulary paragraph, two sections later, states: "`merged` means you also completed claim release and run-dir archival directly (that procedure's Step 4) — but not worktree removal..."

A dispatched second-call agent hit this directly on 2026-09-18: it completed claim release but treated the explicit, outcome-enumerated "do NOT archive… on any outcome (merged, …)" sentence as controlling, and left the run directory unarchived, flagging the contradiction back to the dispatching session rather than guessing. The dispatching session then closed and archived the run directory manually. No data was lost, but every future `pr-first` + `merged` second call will hit the same ambiguity and (correctly, per the more specific sentence a careful reader would find) either skip archival or have to stop and ask, unless one of the two paragraphs is fixed to agree with the other.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Reconcile the two paragraphs in `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s second-call template so they agree on whether the second call archives the run directory when `OUTCOME: merged` under `integration-model: pr-first`.
- [ ] If the outcome-vocabulary paragraph is correct (the second call does archive on `merged`), the "Working directory" paragraph's blanket "on any outcome (merged, armed, ...)" list should drop `merged` (and possibly `ready-to-merge`, if `local-merge`'s labeling-only stop also doesn't archive) or otherwise carve out the exception explicitly.
- [ ] If the "Working directory" paragraph is correct (the dispatching session always archives, even on `merged`), the outcome-vocabulary paragraph's "run-dir archival directly" clause should be removed or corrected to say the dispatching session does it instead.
- [ ] Cross-check `skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` (cited by the outcome-vocabulary paragraph as "that procedure's Step 4") for which behavior it actually documents, and align both `task-prompt.md` paragraphs to match it rather than picking arbitrarily.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `task-prompt.md`'s second-call template no longer contains two paragraphs that give opposite instructions for the same case (`OUTCOME: merged` under `pr-first`).
2. A dispatched second-call agent reaching `OUTCOME: merged` has exactly one correct action to take regarding run-dir archival, sourced from a single unambiguous instruction.

## Original request

Filed during a scheduled `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` Routine firing (session `session_01F8C6998UPYjjFT226Ptq5j`), while dispatching group [#1739,#2336] to PR #2596.

Surface: infra

## Current State

On a GitHub Enterprise remote, `wrap-up-pack.js`'s `unblocked` probe always reports `ok: false`, and `resolve-blockers.js`, `materialize.js`, and `preflight-records.js` fail with "Could not resolve to a Repository" unless the caller both exports `GH_HOST=<enterprise host>` and passes `--repo owner/name` — the plugin never derives host or repo from `origin`. #2425 fixed the `--repo` half of the pack probe; the `GH_HOST` half and the three sibling CLIs remain unfixed as of 6.123.0. Confirmed against the current files: none of `wrap-up-pack.js`/`resolve-blockers.js`/`materialize.js`/`preflight-records.js` reference `GH_HOST` or `nameWithOwner` today.

A private project hosted on a GitHub Enterprise host (origin `https://<enterprise-host>/<org>/<repo>.git`) running `/claude-tweaks:flow` with `work-backend: github-issues` hits this on every wrap-up: the fact pack's `unblocked` probe fails ("could not resolve owner/repo — pass --repo owner/name"), forcing the operator to re-run `resolve-blockers.js` by hand with `GH_HOST` exported and `--repo` passed; `materialize.js` fails the same way at every spec boundary even with `--repo` given, since `gh` never infers the host outside a clone.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a shared helper that derives `{host, ownerRepo}` once from `git remote get-url origin` (or `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` run inside the checkout)
- [ ] Thread the derived `GH_HOST` env var and `--repo owner/name` flag into every child `gh` call in `wrap-up-pack.js`'s `unblocked` probe, `resolve-blockers.js`, `materialize.js`, and `preflight-records.js`
- [ ] Have each of the four CLIs print the derived repo/host so a mismatch is visible to the operator

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a GitHub Enterprise remote, `wrap-up-pack.js`'s `unblocked` probe, `resolve-blockers.js`, `materialize.js`, and `preflight-records.js` all resolve the correct repository with no manually exported `GH_HOST` or passed `--repo`
- [ ] Existing github.com-hosted behavior is unchanged (no regression when there's no enterprise host to derive)
- [ ] `npm test` passes, including new coverage for the derivation helper

## Technical Approach

Add one small derivation helper (host + owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin`, falling back to `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` run inside the checkout) and call it once per invocation in each of the four CLIs, exporting `GH_HOST` and passing `--repo` to every child `gh` call those files make — the same shape #2425 already applied to `wrap-up-pack.js`'s `--repo` half, extended to cover `GH_HOST` there and both flags in the three sibling CLIs.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/wrap-up-pack.js` — the `unblocked` probe; already has partial `--repo` handling from #2425 to extend with `GH_HOST`
- `plugin/bin/resolve-blockers.js` — needs both `GH_HOST` and `--repo` derivation
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js` — needs both `GH_HOST` and `--repo` derivation
- `plugin/bin/preflight-records.js` — needs both `GH_HOST` and `--repo` derivation

## Gotchas

- `gh` does not infer the host outside a clone — a derived `GH_HOST` must be exported into the child process environment, not just computed and discarded.
- Keep the github.com case a true no-op: deriving and passing `--repo`/`GH_HOST` unconditionally must not change behavior (or introduce a new failure mode) for the common non-Enterprise case.

## Original request

wrap-up-pack / resolve-blockers / materialize / preflight-records: on a GitHub Enterprise remote the host is never derived, so every child gh call needs GH_HOST exported by hand

**Summary:** On a GitHub Enterprise remote, `wrap-up-pack.js`'s `unblocked` probe always reports `ok: false`, and `resolve-blockers.js`, `materialize.js` and `preflight-records.js` fail with "Could not resolve to a Repository" unless the caller both exports `GH_HOST=<enterprise host>` and passes `--repo owner/name` — the plugin never derives host or repo from `origin`. (#2425 fixed the `--repo` half of the pack probe; the `GH_HOST` half and the sibling CLIs remain on 6.123.0.)

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `bin/wrap-up-pack.js` (unblocked probe), `bin/resolve-blockers.js`, `bin/materialize.js`, `bin/preflight-records.js`

**Use case:** A private project hosted on a GitHub Enterprise host (origin `https://<enterprise-host>/<org>/<repo>.git`) running `/claude-tweaks:flow` with `work-backend: github-issues`. Every wrap-up's fact pack shows the `unblocked` probe failing ("could not resolve owner/repo — pass --repo owner/name"), so the operator re-runs `resolve-blockers.js` by hand with `GH_HOST` exported and `--repo` passed; `materialize.js` fails the same way at every spec boundary until invoked with `GH_HOST` set, even with `--repo` given — `gh` does not infer the host outside a clone. Suggested behaviour: derive owner/repo AND host once from `git remote get-url origin` (or `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` run inside the checkout) and pass `--repo` plus `GH_HOST` to every child `gh` call; have the pack print the derived repo so a mismatch is visible.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.123.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

#2492 confirmed that `/claude-tweaks:flow`'s Step 2.8 claim step (`bin/claim-targets.js`, or its MCP equivalent) has no mechanical backstop: a `/flow #2322 build,test` dispatch completed a full build+test pass with no `claims/issue-2322.json` blob ever written on `claims-registry`, and none of `flow/claim-targets.md`'s documented skip-guard conditions applied to that dispatch shape — the call was simply never made. `bin/claim-targets.js`'s own write path is not the gap (`tests/bin-lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.test.js` already covers create-only/conditional/contested/transient/unverified-write-back cases in depth, including the write-then-verify race #2073 closed). #2492 closed the doc-only half of this (claim-targets.md now mandates a `decisions.md` log line — `AUTO ... Step 2.8: claimed #{n}` — on every successful claim, both transports), but nothing yet enforces that the claim step actually ran before a build proceeds. This mirrors a failure class the codebase has already solved once: `bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`'s `checkBookkeepingStampsGate` denies the next covered write until `record-worktree` and (under `integration-model: pr-first`) the PR-early draft-PR open have landed — added after IL-131 (a build agent skipping mandatory bookkeeping) recurred on #893. The claim step has no equivalent gate.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Extend `checkBookkeepingStampsGate` (or add a sibling gate using the same materialize-commit-sentinel + `runState`-cached-exemption pattern) to require, once this run's materialize commit has landed and `work-backend: github-issues`, that `decisions.md` carries the `Step 2.8: claimed #{n}` log line (mirroring the existing `hasLoggedPrDegrade` PR-stamp check) before allowing the next covered write — denying with a remediation message that names the missing claim, the same shape the worktree/PR denials already use.
- [ ] Thread a `claimExempt`-style cache field into `run-state.json` (mirroring `prExempt`) so this new check pays its cost once per run, not on every covered call.
- [ ] Add unit tests for the new check sized like the existing `checkBookkeepingStampsGate` coverage (the PR-stamp branch's own test file is the pattern to follow) — cover: claim logged → allow; claim missing after materialize → deny; `work-backend: local-files` → exempt (no claim infra); foreign-owned run → warn, not deny (matching the existing foreign-session downgrade).
- [ ] Update `docs/hooks.md`'s bookkeeping-stamps gate section and `flow/claim-targets.md`'s "Known gap" note (added by #2492) to point at the shipped mechanism instead of describing it as an open gap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `/flow #{n} build,test` dispatch whose Step 2.8 claim step is skipped (no `Step 2.8: claimed #{n}` line in `decisions.md`) is denied at its next covered write by the mechanical gate, with a remediation message — not silently allowed to proceed to a full build with no claim on record.
- [ ] `work-backend: local-files` runs, and runs where the claim log line is present, are unaffected (no new false-deny).
- [ ] `npm test` passes, including the new gate tests.

## Technical Approach

Mirror `checkBookkeepingStampsGate`'s existing PR-stamp branch shape (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`): once the run's materialize commit is detected as landed and `work-backend: github-issues`, grep this run's `decisions.md` for a `Step 2.8: claimed #{n}` line before allowing the next covered write; deny with a remediation message naming the missing claim when absent. Cache the outcome per run in `run-state.json` (a new `claimExempt` field, mirroring the existing `prExempt` field) so the check reads `decisions.md` at most once per run rather than on every covered call. `work-backend: local-files` exempts unconditionally (no claim infra exists on that driver). A foreign-owned run (this session isn't the run's own owner) downgrades to a warning, matching the existing foreign-session posture the PR-stamp branch already uses — never a hard deny on state this session didn't create.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — add the new claim-stamp branch to `checkBookkeepingStampsGate`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — read/cache `run-state.json`'s new `claimExempt` field alongside `prExempt`
- `tests/hooks-bookkeeping-stamps-gate.test.js` — new test cases for the claim-stamp branch
- `docs/hooks.md` — update the bookkeeping-stamps gate section to document the new branch
- `plugin/skills/flow/claim-targets.md` — replace the "Known gap" note with a pointer at the shipped gate

## Gotchas

- The gate must key off `work-backend: github-issues` specifically — `local-files` has no claims infrastructure at all, so an unconditional gate would false-deny every local-files run.
- A foreign-owned run (this session isn't the run's own owner) must warn, not deny, mirroring the existing PR-stamp branch's foreign-session downgrade — the gate must not block a session that isn't responsible for the missing claim.
- Cache the check's outcome in `run-state.json` once landed, so a long multi-write build doesn't re-grep `decisions.md` on every covered call.

## Original request

Mechanically enforce flow Step 2.8's claim write (follow-up from #2492)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:flow #N {step-subset}` resolves whether to adopt an existing pipeline run
directory or create a fresh one based purely on whether the `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` env var is set
(`skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md`'s "Adopting an inherited run directory" section, cases 1-5).
When it is unset -- the common shape for a human re-invoking `/flow #N review,polish,wrap-up` by
hand, days or sessions after `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s first call (`build,test`) -- resolution
falls straight to case 5 (create fresh), with no check of whether the target record already has
a live claim or an open PR carrying a `claude-tweaks-run:` marker.

`steps-and-gates.md`'s own "Intentional two-call consumer" section documents the resume contract
dispatch relies on: both calls must share one run directory via `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` passed inline
on the command line, since a dispatched agent inherits no environment. That contract assumes the
caller always knows to pass it. A human resuming manually has no way to know this is required
unless they happen to notice the record's PR body's own "Resume" line -- a convention that exists
(`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`) but is never surfaced or enforced by `/flow` itself at the
point it would matter (before minting a second run).

Observed instance: a SessionStart hook's unrelated "unfinished pipeline run" notice happened to
name the record and its PR, which is what surfaced the correct resume command in that session --
but that hook is not guaranteed to fire in every session, and nothing in `/flow`'s own
step-argument resolution checks the target record/issue for a live claim or open PR before
defaulting to case 5. Falling through to case 5 on this shape opens a second draft PR/branch
alongside the real one instead of resuming it.

## Deliverables

- Before `/flow`'s step-argument resolution falls through to case 5 (create fresh) on a
  step-subset invocation -- no `build` in the resolved step list, and `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` unset --
  check the named record(s) for a live claim (`_shared/issue-claims.md`'s claim-blob read) or an
  open PR whose body carries a `claude-tweaks-run:` marker.
- When either signal is found, either auto-adopt that run directory (preferred, when the signal
  unambiguously names one run) or surface a prompt naming the candidate run directory / PR and
  asking whether to resume it or proceed with a fresh run -- never silently mint a duplicate.
- When neither signal is found, proceed to case 5 exactly as today -- this check must not slow
  down or change behavior for a genuinely fresh, first-call invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/claude-tweaks:flow #N review,polish,wrap-up` (no `build` in the step list, `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`
  unset) against a record with a live claim or an open `claude-tweaks-run:`-marked PR no longer
  mints a second run directory/draft PR -- it either resumes the existing run or asks first.
- `/claude-tweaks:flow #N {step-subset}` against a record with **no** live claim and **no**
  open marked PR behaves exactly as before this fix -- proceeds to case 5, no new prompt, no
  added latency for the common fresh-invocation case.
- The check reuses `_shared/issue-claims.md`'s existing claim-read mechanics and the PR-body
  marker convention `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` already documents -- no new detection
  mechanism invented for this fix.
- A test exercises the specific shape this record reports: step-subset invocation, no `build`,
  `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` unset, target record carrying a live claim or marked open PR.

## Technical Approach

Add the live-claim/open-PR check as a new gate inside `flow/steps-and-gates.md`'s adoption
resolution, positioned before case 5's creation path -- the resolution already branches on
`PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` presence and `preflight.json`'s `adoption.value.case`, so this is an additional
branch in the same decision point, not a parallel mechanism. Read the target record's claim state
per `_shared/issue-claims.md`'s "Reading claim state," and search open PRs whose
`closingIssuesReferences` name the target record for the `claude-tweaks-run:` body marker
(`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s PR-open template). `flow/SKILL.md` Step 3 is the entry
point that reaches this resolution; wire the new gate there or in `steps-and-gates.md` directly,
whichever the existing case-1-through-5 branching structure makes the smaller diff.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md` -- the "Adopting an inherited run directory" section,
  case 5's creation fallback
- `plugin/skills/flow/SKILL.md` -- Step 3, where step-argument resolution reaches this branch
- `plugin/skills/_shared/issue-claims.md` -- the claim-read mechanics to reuse
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` -- the `claude-tweaks-run:` PR-body marker
  convention to reuse

## Gotchas

- This check must stay cheap and skip-fast for the ordinary case (no claim, no marked PR) --
  every step-subset invocation with `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` unset pays this check's cost, including
  the vastly more common genuinely-fresh first-call shape.
- Dedup-checked manually at filing time against #1013/#1129/#1858/#1826 -- none match (those
  cover `config.yml`/PR-early bootstrap being skipped on adoption, not a fresh duplicate run
  being minted when `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is unset on a step-subset invocation).
- **Related:** #2413 ("flow's Step 3 Manifesto did not write config.yml on a two-call dispatch
  resume") is topically adjacent -- same two-call resume area -- but is a distinct defect (a
  missed `config.yml` write on an already-correctly-adopted run), not a duplicate of this gap.

## Original request

flow: bare resume invocation (no PIPELINE_RUN_DIR) can mint a duplicate run over a live one

**Summary:** `/claude-tweaks:flow #N {step-subset}` with no `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` set and no `build` in the step list falls through adoption case 5 (create fresh) instead of checking whether the record already has a live claim/open PR to resume.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** skills/flow (SKILL.md Step 3, steps-and-gates.md's "Adopting an inherited run directory" section)

**Use case:** Resuming a `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`-orchestrated two-call handoff (`build,test` then `review,polish,wrap-up`) by hand, days or sessions after the first call, with no `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` carried forward in the invoking session's environment. `steps-and-gates.md`'s own documented resume contract (the "Intentional two-call consumer" section) assumes the caller always passes `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` inline -- but a human re-invoking `/flow #N review,polish,wrap-up` from a fresh session has no way to know that's required unless they happen to notice the record's PR body's own "Resume" line (a convention that exists but is never surfaced or enforced by `/flow` itself). Per adoption case 5, an unset `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` on this exact invocation shape falls straight to "create a fresh run directory," which would open a second draft PR/branch alongside the real one rather than resuming it. In this instance a SessionStart hook's unrelated "unfinished pipeline run" notice happened to name the record and its PR, which is what surfaced the correct resume command -- but that hook is not guaranteed to fire in every session, and nothing in `/flow`'s own step-argument resolution checks the target record/issue for a live claim or open PR before defaulting to case 5.

**Definition:** Needed -- before falling through to case 5 on a step-subset invocation (no `build` in the resolved step list) with `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` unset, check the named record(s) for a live claim (`_shared/issue-claims.md`) or an open PR whose body carries a `claude-tweaks-run:` marker, and either auto-adopt that run directory or surface a prompt naming it -- rather than silently minting a duplicate.

**Plugin version:** 6.123.0

---
Filed via /claude-tweaks:feedback (headless continuation, dedup-checked manually against #1013/#1129/#1858/#1826 -- none match: those cover config.yml/PR-early bootstrap being skipped on adoption, not a fresh duplicate run being minted when PIPELINE_RUN_DIR is unset on a step-subset invocation).

Surface: infra

**Related:** #1728, #1734, #1738, #1811, #1826, #1841, #1892, #1982, #2032, #2051, #2081, #2226, #2228, #2229, #2230, #2231, #2240, #2330, #2332 (near-duplicate screen hits — shared file-path/anchor mentions only, not confirmed duplicates of this record's own topic)

## Current State

In one seven-spec multi-record run, eight commits failed with
`fatal: Unable to create '<repo>/.git/index.lock': File exists`. The lock holder was a sibling
agent's git call or a PostToolUse hook in the same checkout, never a stale process — every one of
them succeeded on a retry a couple of seconds later. The run only got through because the ad-hoc
ledger-append scripts written for it grew their own 2-second retry loop; nothing in the plugin
provided one.

The plugin's own commit call sites run `git commit` through `execFileSync` with no retry at all:

- `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `runGit(['commit', '-m', '[reconcile] archive run …'])`
- `bin/lib/release/run.js` — `deps.git(['commit', '-m', 'Release v… — …'])`
- `bin/release-local.js` — `deps.git(['commit', '-m', 'chore(release): v…'])`

A transient index-lock collision at any of these surfaces as a hard failure of a reconcile or
release step, in exactly the multi-agent setting the plugin is built for (parallel dispatch,
worktrees, hooks running git in the background). The sanctioned run-dir writers

Surface: infra

## Current State

`_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` is the dispatch-correctness contract: minimal input, the
four-word status line, the A/B/C output templates, model-profile selection, and the third-party
exemption. Every mechanical check it defines is a check on the **shape** of the reply.

In one seven-spec run, a review lens agent (lens 3f, first dispatch) returned six findings, each
citing a file and line numbers, after **zero tool calls** — it read nothing. Its status line was
well-formed and its output template was filled in correctly, so every check the contract defines
passed. It was caught only because the orchestrator happened to inspect the agent's tool-use count
by hand, and re-dispatched a fresh agent (3f-B). The contract that exists specifically to make N
agents independent evidence rather than N echoes has no rule that would have caught it.

The principle is already stated elsewhere in the project, just not where dispatch correctness is
defined: CLAUDE.md's test-count rule ("never accept a subagent's self-reported pass/fail numbers as
a run … a fabricated report is indistinguishable from load here"), and a standing memory entry
recording that agents fabricate fix reports with zero diff. Neither reaches a dispatch site, because
every dispatch site inherits its discipline from the contract file, not from CLAUDE.md's prose.

`subagent-stop.js` already reads the dispatched agent's own transcript (`agent_transcript_path`) to
grade the status line, so the tool-use count for a final reply is derivable at the same seam — this
check need not stay a manual orchestrator habit.

## Deliverables

- State the rule in `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`: a verdict, findings list, or
  pass/fail claim from an agent whose transcript contains zero tool calls is a **failed
  dispatch**, never evidence. The caller re-dispatches a fresh agent (never resumes the same
  one — the 529/stall precedent: 0/5 resumes succeeded) and never aggregates the reply.
- Put it in the contract's aggregation guidance so every dispatch site enumerated in CLAUDE.md's
  Subagent Contract section inherits it by citation, with no site restating it (CLAUDE.md's
  cross-reference rule). Extend the Exemption section's caller-side normalization sentence to
  name it explicitly: a third-party agent is exempt from the contract, but the caller still
  rejects a zero-tool-use verdict at the boundary.
- Add the mechanical assist at the `subagent-stop.js` seam: count tool calls in the graded
  agent transcript and log a distinct event kind (e.g. `zero-tool-use-verdict`) when a final
  reply carries a verdict shape with no tool call behind it, so the failure is visible in
  `events.jsonl` rather than depending on an orchestrator noticing. Add the kind to
  `bin/friction-events.js` and `reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens vocabulary block.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` states the zero-tool-use rule, what makes it a failed
   dispatch, and that the remedy is a fresh dispatch rather than a resume.
2. Every dispatch site listed in CLAUDE.md's Subagent Contract section reaches the rule by citation;
   a repo-wide grep finds no site restating it inline.
3. A fixture transcript whose final assistant turn carries a well-formed status line and a findings
   table, with zero tool-use blocks, logs a `zero-tool-use-verdict` event; an otherwise identical
   transcript with one tool-use block logs nothing. Both directions asserted in
   `tests/bin-lib/hooks/`.
4. `node --test tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` passes with the new kind, and `npm test`
   passes.

## Non-Goals

- Grading intermediate turns. The rule applies to the reply the caller consumes, not to every turn a
  long-running dispatch produces (that scoping question is #2041's).
- Any judgment about *how much* tool use is enough. Zero is the only threshold this record sets.

## Technical Approach

Two coupled changes, per the Deliverables above:

1. **Contract text.** Add the zero-tool-use rule to `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s
   aggregation guidance — worded as a hard rule (a zero-tool-use verdict is a failed dispatch,
   never evidence; remedy is a fresh dispatch, never a resume of the same agent). Extend the
   Exemption section's existing caller-side normalization sentence to state explicitly that this
   check applies at the boundary even to a third-party agent otherwise exempt from the contract's
   other structural requirements.
2. **Mechanical assist.** In `bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js`, at the same seam that already reads
   `agent_transcript_path` to grade the status line, count tool-use blocks in the final graded
   turn. When the count is zero and the reply shape carries a verdict/findings/pass-fail claim,
   log a `zero-tool-use-verdict` event (distinct kind, alongside the existing `contract-violation`
   kind) rather than silently passing shape-only checks. Wire the new kind through
   `bin/friction-events.js`'s aggregation and `reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens vocabulary
   block, mirroring how the existing `contract-violation`/`variant` kinds are already wired.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — add the zero-tool-use rule to the
  aggregation guidance and the Exemption section
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` — count tool-use blocks in the graded transcript, log
  `zero-tool-use-verdict`
- `plugin/bin/friction-events.js` — aggregate the new event kind
- `plugin/skills/reflect/full-mode.md` — Friction lens vocabulary block, new kind name
- `tests/bin-lib/hooks/` — new fixture-transcript test (zero-tool-use vs. one-tool-use cases)
- `tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` — cover the new kind name

## Gotchas

- This rule targets the *final* reply the caller consumes — do not apply it to intermediate
  turns of a long-running dispatch (explicitly out of scope per Non-Goals; #2041 owns that
  broader scoping question).
- Don't invent a nonzero tool-use threshold ("at least N calls") — this record sets a strict
  zero/nonzero line only; anything more nuanced is future scope, not this record's.
- The contract-text change and the mechanical-assist change are both required by the Acceptance
  Criteria — landing only the mechanical assist without updating the contract text leaves every
  dispatch site's own prompt-level discipline unchanged, and landing only the contract text
  without the hook change leaves the failure mode dependent on manual orchestrator vigilance
  again, the exact gap this record exists to close.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` logs one `contract-violation` event per graded reply that fails its
three-tier status detection. `bin/friction-events.js` returns that kind unweighted, and
`reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens judges a run's proportionality from the aggregate count.

One seven-spec multi-record pipeline run produced **82** `contract-violation` events (0 carrying
`variant: 'lenient'`). Classifying every event by its own recorded `firstLine`:

| Population | Count | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Foreign status contract | 21 (26%) | `firstLine` is exactly a verdict word from a *different* declared contract — `APPROVED`, `NEEDS_FIXES`, `ADDRESSED`, `VERIFIED` — from reviewer and fix-verification dispatches whose own prompt template declares that vocabulary |
| Non-final / mid-turn narration | 55 (67%) | `"Let me finalize the review."`, `"### Spec Compliance"`, `"Working tree clean, commit created successfully."` — turns that were never the dispatch's final reply |
| Genuine contract violation | 6 (7%) | The narration-before-the-status-word shape the contract's two `WRONG:` examples target |

So the lens reported "82 contract violations" for a run whose real contract-compliance failure count
was at most 6, against 2 `ask-user-question` stops over 201 first-parent commits.

The foreign-contract population is already named in `subagent-stop.js`'s own header as **known
false-positive source #1** — "a dispatch whose own template specifies a different status contract …
is logged here even though nothing was actually violated — the detector has no way to know a
dispatch declared a different contract" — with no record tracking it and no mechanism proposed.
#750 (closed) fixed only the literal `- **Status:** WORD` bullet shape via `LENIENT_RE`; #2265's
tier-2 lenient window matches only a contract word at the **start** of a line, so neither reaches a
reply whose first token is a verdict word belonging to another contract.

The original reflect finding read the 82 as one shape (narration before the status word) and
proposed widening detection to the first five lines. That premise does not survive measurement:
widening the window would move 6 events, not 82, and #2265's first-or-last-3-line window already
covers most of that shape. The defect is population conflation, not detector tolerance.

## Deliverables

- Let a dispatcher declare that its agents answer under a different status contract, so
  `subagent-stop.js` skips grading them — keyed off state the dispatch already writes (the
  run-dir dispatch record) rather than a new prompt convention — and stop logging known
  false-positive source #1 as a violation at all.
- Where grading still applies, separate the populations **at the event**: carry
  `variant: 'foreign-contract' | 'non-final' | 'violation'` on the logged event (alongside the
  existing `'lenient'`), so the count a reader sees is not a sum of three unrelated things.
- `bin/friction-events.js` reports the genuine violation count distinctly from the other
  variants; `reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens text names the genuine count as the number it
  judges aggregate volume on, and `tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` covers any new
  variant names.
- Remove the resolved half of known-false-positive source #1 from `subagent-stop.js`'s header
  comment, with a recorded removal condition for anything deliberately left as a shim (CLAUDE.md's
  no-indefinite-compatibility-shim rule).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A final reply whose first line is a verdict word from a dispatcher-declared alternate contract
   logs no `contract-violation`, or logs one carrying `variant: 'foreign-contract'` — proven by a
   unit test feeding `detectStatus`/the hook a reply beginning `APPROVED` under a declared alternate
   contract, and by an orthogonal case (an unrelated third vocabulary present) that still grades.
2. Replaying this run's 82 recorded `firstLine` values through the classifier yields a genuine
   (`variant: 'violation'`) count of at most 6; the foreign-contract and non-final variants account
   for the rest.
3. `friction-events.js --run <dir>` reports the genuine count separately, and
   `reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens reads that number rather than the conflated total.
4. `node --test tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` passes with the new variant names, and
   `npm test` passes.

## Non-Goals

- The non-final/mid-turn population's own fix — #2041 owns scoping the check to a dispatch's
  terminal reply. This record's `variant` separation makes that population *visible*; it does not
  pre-empt #2041's mechanism.
- Widening the status-word detection window further. #2265 already covers the off-position
  line-start shape, and the measurement above shows the remaining tolerance gap is 6 events.

## Technical Approach

Two independent mechanisms, per the Deliverables above:

1. **Declared-contract skip.** Identify what state a dispatch already writes to the run
   directory that names its agents' declared status vocabulary (the dispatch record
   `subagent-output-contract.md`-following skills already write per-dispatch metadata for).
   `subagent-stop.js` reads that state for the dispatch a graded reply belongs to and skips
   grading entirely when the declared contract differs from the harness's own three-tier
   vocabulary — this is a detection-time skip, not a post-hoc reclassification, so it also stops
   the event from being logged at all (cleaner than tagging it `foreign-contract` after the
   fact, per the Deliverables' own "stop logging ... as a violation at all" wording).
2. **Variant tagging for the remainder.** For replies that do get graded, extend the logged
   event shape with `variant: 'foreign-contract' | 'non-final' | 'violation'` (alongside the
   existing `'lenient'` value from #2265/#750) — this variant reflects the classification
   observed in this record's own measurement table, applied going forward. `friction-events.js`
   aggregates and reports the `'violation'` count separately from the others;
   `reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens text is updated to read that field instead of the
   conflated total.

### Key Files

- `bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` — declared-contract skip logic, `variant` field on the logged
  event, header-comment update removing the resolved half of known false-positive source #1
- `bin/friction-events.js` — report the `'violation'` variant count distinctly from the others
- `reflect/full-mode.md` — Friction lens reads the genuine-violation count, not the conflated
  total
- `tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` — cover the new variant names

## Gotchas

- Do not conflate this record's `variant` separation with #2041's own fix (scoping the
  three-tier check to a dispatch's terminal reply only) — they are complementary, not
  overlapping: this record makes the non-final population *visible and separately counted*; it
  does not stop it from being logged as a distinct variant.
- The declared-contract skip must be keyed off state the dispatch itself already writes, not a
  new prompt-authoring convention — inventing a new declaration mechanism here would mean every
  existing dispatch template needs updating just to keep working correctly.
- When removing the resolved half of `subagent-stop.js`'s header-comment note about known
  false-positive source #1, keep whatever part (if any) still applies after this fix — don't
  delete the whole comment if only part of the false-positive source is actually resolved.

## Original request

## Current State

three-tier status detection. `bin/friction-events.js` returns that kind unweighted, and

| Genuine contract violation | 6 (7%) | The narration-before-the-status-word shape the contract's two `WRONG:` examples target |

So the lens reported "82 contract violations" for a run whose real contract-compliance failure count
was at most 6, against 2 `ask-user-question` stops over 201 first-parent commits.

The foreign-contract population is already named in `subagent-stop.js`'s own header as **known
false-positive source #1** — "a dispatch whose own template specifies a different status contract …
is logged here even though nothing was actually violated — the detector has no way to know a
dispatch declared a different contract" — with no record tracking it and no mechanism proposed.
#750 (closed) fixed only the literal `- **Status:** WORD` bullet shape via `LENIENT_RE`; #2265's
tier-2 lenient window matches only a contract word at the **start** of a line, so neither reaches a
reply whose first token is a verdict word belonging to another contract.

The original reflect finding read the 82 as one shape (narration before the status word) and
proposed widening detection to the first five lines. That premise does not survive measurement:
widening the window would move 6 events, not 82, and #2265's first-or-last-3-line window already
covers most of that shape. The defect is population conflation, not detector tolerance.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Let a dispatcher declare that its agents answer under a different status contract, so
      `subagent-stop.js` skips grading them — keyed off state the dispatch already writes (the
      run-dir dispatch record) rather than a new prompt convention — and stop logging known
      false-positive source #1 as a violation at all.
- [ ] Where grading still applies, separate the populations **at the event**: carry
      `variant: 'foreign-contract' | 'non-final' | 'violation'` on the logged event (alongside the
      existing `'lenient'`), so the count a reader sees is not a sum of three unrelated things.
- [ ] `bin/friction-events.js` reports the genuine violation count distinctly from the other
      variants; `reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens text names the genuine count as the number it
      judges aggregate volume on, and `tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` covers any new
      variant names.
- [ ] Remove the resolved half of known-false-positive source #1 from `subagent-stop.js`'s header
      comment, with a recorded removal condition for anything deliberately left as a shim (CLAUDE.md's
      no-indefinite-compatibility-shim rule).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A final reply whose first line is a verdict word from a dispatcher-declared alternate contract
   logs no `contract-violation`, or logs one carrying `variant: 'foreign-contract'` — proven by a
   unit test feeding `detectStatus`/the hook a reply beginning `APPROVED` under a declared alternate
   contract, and by an orthogonal case (an unrelated third vocabulary present) that still grades.
2. Replaying this run's 82 recorded `firstLine` values through the classifier yields a genuine
   (`variant: 'violation'`) count of at most 6; the foreign-contract and non-final variants account
   for the rest.
3. `friction-events.js --run <dir>` reports the genuine count separately, and
   `reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens reads that number rather than the conflated total.
4. `node --test tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` passes with the new variant names, and
   `npm test` passes.

## Non-Goals

- The non-final/mid-turn population's own fix — #2041 owns scoping the check to a dispatch's
  terminal reply. This record's `variant` separation makes that population *visible*; it does not
  pre-empt #2041's mechanism.
- Widening the status-word detection window further. #2265 already covers the off-position
  line-start shape, and the measurement above shows the remaining tolerance gap is 6 events.

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`. `recordLabels`
(confirmed, line 397) changed from a sequential loop to an unbounded `Promise.all` fan-out of
`gh issue view` calls, with no test added for the concurrency or partial-failure semantics.

`tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js`'s only addition in this range is a
`resolveRecords`/`headerRecords` export check — nothing pins that a mid-list `gh` failure still
surfaces correctly, or that N is bounded (an unbounded fan-out over a large record list could hit
`gh`'s own rate limiting).

## Deliverables

- Add a test covering a mid-list `gh issue view` failure in the `Promise.all` fan-out — confirm
  the failure surfaces (doesn't get silently swallowed) and confirm what happens to the other
  in-flight calls.
- Consider whether the fan-out needs a concurrency bound for large record lists.

## Acceptance Criteria

A test exists that fails a middle call in the fan-out and asserts the overall behavior (error
propagation or partial-result handling, whichever is intended) explicitly.

## Technical Approach

Read `recordLabels`'s actual current behavior first (line 397's surrounding function) to
determine what it's *supposed* to do on a partial failure — `Promise.all` itself rejects the
whole batch on the first rejection, so unless the mapped callback already catches per-record
errors internally, a single `gh issue view` failure currently aborts the entire `recordLabels`
call for every record, not just the failing one. Write a test with a fake `gh` runner that fails
on (e.g.) the third of five record lookups and assert whichever behavior is actually intended:
either the whole call rejects (document that this is deliberate, given the caller's own
error-handling expectations) or partial results are still usable (in which case the current code
needs an `allSettled`-style fix, not just a test). For the concurrency-bound question: check
whether this codebase's existing gh-api-module-pattern convention or a sibling call site already
establishes a bound for similar fan-outs (e.g. a `concurrency` option, or a batch-size cap) and
apply the same convention here if large record lists are a realistic scenario for `wrap-up`'s own
callers (multi-spec runs with many records).

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `recordLabels` (line 397), possibly needs an
  `allSettled`-style rewrite or a concurrency bound depending on the investigation above
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js` — add the mid-list-failure test

## Gotchas

- Don't assume `Promise.all`'s all-or-nothing rejection semantics are a bug — they may be the
  deliberate, correct behavior for this call site (a wrap-up pack build that can't tolerate a
  partial label set). Read the surrounding code and its caller's own error handling before
  concluding a fix (vs. just documenting+testing the existing all-or-nothing behavior) is needed.
- If a concurrency bound is added, verify it doesn't reintroduce the sequential-loop performance
  regression this `Promise.all` change was presumably meant to fix in the first place — a bound
  should cap peak concurrency, not collapse back to strictly sequential.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`.
New failure reasons `work-twin-conflict` (confirmed, ~line 684) and
`work-twin-resolve-failed[-partial-revert]` are never tracked toward residue escalation, so a
genuinely diverged work twin is skipped silently on every reconcile pass forever — no streak, no
issue filed.

`trackArchiveResult` (confirmed, ~line 1083) early-returns `if (result.reason !== 'move-failed')
return;` before reaching `trackResidue`, and `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (confirmed, line 1030)
is `new Set(['no-worktree', 'no-branch', 'no-pr'])` — it doesn't include either new twin reason.

## Deliverables

Extend `trackArchiveResult`/`STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (or add an equivalent path) so a
`work-twin-conflict`/`work-twin-resolve-failed[-partial-revert]` result accumulates toward the
same residue-escalation streak as the existing structurally-stuck reasons, rather than being
silently dropped every pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

A reconcile run that repeatedly hits `work-twin-conflict` on the same run dir eventually
escalates (streak-based issue filing), the same way a repeated `no-worktree`/`no-branch`/`no-pr`
result does today.

## Technical Approach

Widen `trackArchiveResult`'s early-return guard (~line 1083) from the single literal
`result.reason !== 'move-failed'` to also accept `work-twin-conflict` and
`work-twin-resolve-failed`/`work-twin-resolve-failed-partial-revert`, routing them into the same
`trackResidue(root, repoSlug, {reason}, dir, { failed: true, lastError: result.lastError },
{ escalate })` call the `move-failed` path already uses — reuse the existing choke point rather
than duplicating escalation logic. Decide whether the twin reasons need their own `reason` key
passed to `trackResidue` (distinct from `'move-failed'`) so `escalate-residue.js`'s filed-issue
title/body correctly names "work-twin-conflict" rather than generically reusing "move-failed" —
this affects how a human reading the escalated issue understands what actually went wrong, so
prefer the more specific reason string.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — widen `trackArchiveResult`'s reason guard
  (~line 1083) to also route `work-twin-conflict`/`work-twin-resolve-failed[-partial-revert]`
  into `trackResidue`

## Gotchas

- `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (line 1030) governs a *different* mechanism (the
  `isStructurallyStuck()`/`no-branch`-class TTL-based staleness check) than
  `trackArchiveResult`'s own `move-failed`-keyed residue tracking — don't conflate the two; this
  record's fix is about routing the twin reasons into `trackResidue`'s escalation streak, not
  necessarily adding them to `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` itself (which governs a specific,
  separate no-worktree/no-branch/no-pr classification). Verify which mechanism actually needs
  the new reasons before changing both.
- A `work-twin-resolve-failed-partial-revert` is a worse state than a clean `work-twin-conflict`
  (a partially-applied revert) — make sure the escalated issue's body can distinguish the two
  reasons, not just lump them under one generic label, since a human resolving the escalation
  needs to know which situation they're looking at.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/materialize.js`'s `--multi-record-slug` handling (confirmed still present, lines ~306-308)
writes the spec under `path.join(opts.runDir, 'spec-' + opts.multiRecordSlug, 'work')` rather
than `path.join(opts.runDir, 'work')` — an existing test
(`tests/bin-lib/issues/materialize-format.test.js:297`, "materialize CLI: --multi-record-slug
writes under spec-{slug}/work/") documents this as the CLI's own intended contract: `--run-dir`
is expected to be the **parent** directory, and `--multi-record-slug` descends into a per-spec
`spec-{slug}/` subdirectory beneath it.

The reported failure is a **contract mismatch at the call site**, not necessarily a bug in the
CLI's own tested behavior: `flow/materialize.md`'s own documented CLI signature says flatly "the
CLI writes `{--run-dir}/work/{n}-spec.md` exactly under whatever path is passed" — it does not
mention `--multi-record-slug` at all, and does not say when a caller should or shouldn't pass it
during a multi-spec run. `flow/multi-spec.md` (line 113) documents `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` as already
resolving to the per-spec `{parent}/spec-{N}/` subdirectory for a multi-spec run. The reporter's
repro shows a call site materializing the third record of a multi-spec run with
`--run-dir {parent}/spec-C` (already per-spec) **and** `--multi-record-slug A-B-C` together —
under the CLI's own tested contract, that double-supplies the per-spec descent: once via
`--run-dir` already being `spec-C`, and again via `--multi-record-slug` appending a second
`spec-A-B-C` level beneath it, producing
`{parent}/spec-C/spec-A-B-C/work/C-spec.md` instead of the expected
`{parent}/spec-C/work/C-spec.md`.

`opts.multiRecordSlug` has no other use in `materialize.js` besides this one workDir
construction — it carries no other side effect that a fix here would need to preserve.

## Deliverables

- Locate the exact call site (in `/flow`'s or `/build`'s multi-spec materialization sequence)
  that invokes `materialize.js` with both an already-per-spec `--run-dir` and
  `--multi-record-slug` set — determine whether that call site should stop passing
  `--multi-record-slug` (since `--run-dir` has already resolved to the per-spec directory), or
  whether it should instead pass the shared **parent** directory as `--run-dir` and let
  `--multi-record-slug` do the per-spec descent, matching the CLI's own currently-tested
  contract.
- Apply whichever fix resolves the mismatch without breaking the CLI's existing tested contract
  (`materialize-format.test.js:297`) for any caller that correctly relies on the parent+slug
  shape — update that test only if the CLI's contract itself is deliberately changed, with a
  clear reason recorded for the change.
- Update `flow/materialize.md`'s documented CLI signature to state explicitly when
  `--multi-record-slug` should (and should not) be passed alongside `--run-dir`, closing the gap
  that let this mismatch ship silently in the first place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow "#A,#B,#C"` run in `auto` mode with a shared worktree
  materializes each spec's file at `{parent}/spec-{N}/work/{n}-spec.md` — no extra
  `spec-{slug}` nesting level — matching the reporter's own stated expectation and what `/build`'s
  "read it in place" check, the consolidated console's `spec-{N}/work/{n}-spec.md` enumeration,
  and the archive's per-spec `git mv` all already assume.
- `materialize-format.test.js`'s existing `--multi-record-slug` test either still passes
  unchanged (if the fix is call-site-only) or is deliberately updated to reflect a changed CLI
  contract (if the fix changes `materialize.js` itself) — never left silently contradicting the
  new call-site behavior.
- `flow/materialize.md` states the `--run-dir`/`--multi-record-slug` interaction explicitly, so a
  future caller cannot reproduce this same double-nesting by accident.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Grep every call site invoking `materialize.js` with `--multi-record-slug` (already found:
`dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s prompt template — verify whether `/flow`'s own multi-spec sequence,
not just dispatch's fan-out template, has an equivalent invocation) and, for each, determine what
value it actually passes for `--run-dir` at that point in the sequence — a per-spec
`{parent}/spec-{N}` (per `flow/multi-spec.md:113`'s own `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` documentation) or the
shared parent. The fix is whichever of these restores a single level of per-spec nesting:
(a) stop passing `--multi-record-slug` when `--run-dir` already resolved to the per-spec
directory, or (b) pass the parent directory as `--run-dir` and let `--multi-record-slug` do the
descent, matching the CLI's own currently-tested contract. Prefer (a) unless there's a concrete
reason the call site needs the parent path for something else at that same call — changing the
call site is lower blast radius than changing the CLI's own tested contract, since the CLI's
`spec-{slug}` shape may have other current callers this record hasn't traced.

### Key Files

- The identified call site (in `/flow` or `/build`'s multi-spec materialization sequence, or
  `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s prompt template — confirm which is actually implicated by the
  repro) — fix the `--run-dir`/`--multi-record-slug` argument pairing
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js` (~lines 306-308) — only touched if the CLI's own contract is
  deliberately changed instead of the call site
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/materialize-format.test.js` (~line 297) — update only if the CLI
  contract changes
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — document the `--run-dir`/`--multi-record-slug`
  interaction explicitly

## Gotchas

- Do not fix this by simply deleting `--multi-record-slug`'s effect from `materialize.js` without
  checking `materialize-format.test.js:297` and every other call site first — that test currently
  documents the flag's nesting behavior as intentional CLI contract, not a leftover bug; changing
  it silently could break a caller this record hasn't traced.
- Windows path handling: the original report was filed on Windows 11 — verify the fix's path
  joining is platform-neutral (`path.join`, already in use, is fine; just don't introduce a
  hardcoded `/` anywhere while touching this code).

## Original request

**Summary:** With `--multi-record-slug`, `bin/materialize.js` writes the spec under `{run-dir}/spec-{N}/spec-{slug}/work/` instead of `{run-dir}/spec-{N}/work/`.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** bin/materialize.js (`--multi-record-slug`), flow/materialize.md

**Repro steps:**
1. Start a multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow "#A,#B,#C"` run in `auto` mode with a shared worktree (`worktree-always: true`), so the parent run dir holds `spec-A/`, `spec-B/`, `spec-C/`.
2. For the third record, materialize with `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR={parent}/spec-C` and `--multi-record-slug A-B-C`.
3. Look for `{parent}/spec-C/work/C-spec.md`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the materialized file lands at `{PIPELINE_RUN_DIR}/work/{n}-spec.md` — the path `/build`'s "read it in place" check, the consolidated console's `spec-{N}/work/{n}-spec.md` release-claim enumeration and the archive's per-spec `git mv` all expect.
Actual: the multi-record slug is appended as a second `spec-` directory level beneath the per-spec run dir that `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` already names: `{parent}/spec-C/spec-A-B-C/work/C-spec.md`. The file had to be moved by hand (one extra commit) before the build could adopt it.

Observed on plugin 6.114.1, Windows 11, a private project on a GHE remote.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

Surface: infra

## Current State

The PreToolUse worktree-isolation guard (`bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`'s `checkWorktreeRequired`
and its supporting compound-Bash-shape detection) refuses Bash commands it cannot prove are
non-git (runtime-computed paths, heredocs mentioning commits, compound commands) when
`worktree-always: true`. `bin/friction-events.js` recognizes five event kinds (comment at line
~26: `wd-deny`, `gate-denial`, `bookkeeping-stamp-deny`, and others) but this specific refusal
class is not one of them — confirmed still true: no `wd-guard-refusal`-shaped kind exists in
either `friction-events.js` or `pre-tool-use.js` as of this shaping pass. `checkWorktreeRequired`
does call `appendEvent(..., 'gate-denial', ...)` at one point in its own logic, but that call is
scoped to a resolved "owned run" context (per the surrounding comment: "an owned run dir records
nothing here" for the foreign-owned case) — it is not a general log-every-refusal call, which is
consistent with the reporter's direct empirical observation below.

A real run (worktree-always: true, plugin 6.118.0) over one build → test → review → wrap-up cycle
had roughly eight commands refused by this guard — a `sed -n` reading a run-dir path from a shell
variable, a `for` loop over `gh issue list --json` calls, and heredocs mentioning commit hashes —
each rewritten by hand into a plain command or moved to the Write tool. At wrap-up,
`/claude-tweaks:reflect`'s Friction lens ran `friction-events.js --run <run-dir>` and saw 1
`bookkeeping-stamp-deny` and 13 `contract-violation` events, and zero `wd-deny`/`gate-denial` —
the eight guard refusals left no trace, so the lens reported the run as proportionate when the
guard refusals were the operator's most frequent actual stop. The refusal mechanism itself is
already tracked separately (#1798); this record is only about its observability.

## Deliverables

- Log each worktree-isolation guard refusal (the "cannot prove non-git" compound/heredoc/
  runtime-path case, distinct from `checkWorktreeRequired`'s own narrower `gate-denial` path) as
  a new friction event kind — e.g. `wd-guard-refusal` — carrying the refused command's executable
  and the refusal reason.
- Add the new kind to `bin/friction-events.js`'s recognized-kinds list and its aggregation logic.
- Add the new kind to `skills/reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens vocabulary block, so the
  pinned vocabulary test (`tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js`) covers it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree-isolation guard refusal of the "cannot prove non-git" shape (a compound command, a
  heredoc mentioning a commit, or a runtime-computed path) appends a `wd-guard-refusal` event
  (or equivalent new kind) to the active run's `events.jsonl`, distinct from `gate-denial` and
  `wd-deny`.
- `friction-events.js --run <dir>` reports the new kind's count in its aggregate output.
- `reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction lens vocabulary block names the new kind, and
  `node --test tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` passes.
- Replaying this record's own described run (8 guard refusals, 1 `bookkeeping-stamp-deny`, 13
  `contract-violation`) with the fix applied would show 8 `wd-guard-refusal` events, making the
  Friction lens's proportionality judgment reflect the operator's actual experience.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Locate every return point in `checkWorktreeRequired` (and any sibling function in
`pre-tool-use.js` handling the same "cannot prove non-git, fails closed" compound-Bash refusal
class — per that file's own comment at ~line 135, "Fails CLOSED, deliberately: anything this
cannot prove sits under the repo's [isolation boundary]") that produces a deny decision for this
specific refusal shape, as opposed to the already-logged `gate-denial`/`wd-deny` paths. Add an
`appendEvent(runDir, 'wd-guard-refusal', { command: command.slice(0, 200), reason })` call at
each such point, following the exact pattern the existing `gate-denial` call
(`appendEvent(ownedRun.dir, 'gate-denial', { tool: toolName, path: targetPath, ...testTag },
ownedRun.attribution)`) already uses — including its run-dir resolution and any test-tag
handling needed to avoid the test suite's own exercise of this gate polluting a real run's
friction counts (mirroring `friction-events.js`'s existing `gate-denial`+`test===true` skip at
line ~93). Then wire the new kind through `friction-events.js`'s aggregation and
`reflect/full-mode.md`'s vocabulary block the same way the existing five kinds are already wired.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — add the `wd-guard-refusal` event append at the
  compound/heredoc/runtime-path refusal point(s) in `checkWorktreeRequired`
- `plugin/bin/friction-events.js` — recognize and aggregate the new kind (mirror the existing
  `gate-denial` test-tag skip if the same test-pollution risk applies)
- `plugin/skills/reflect/full-mode.md` — Friction lens vocabulary block, new kind name
- `tests/reflect-friction-lens-vocab.test.js` — cover the new kind name

## Gotchas

- Do not conflate this new kind with the existing `gate-denial` event `checkWorktreeRequired`
  already logs for its own narrower, owned-run-scoped case — they're different refusal shapes;
  changing `gate-denial`'s existing meaning would break whatever currently reads it.
- Mirror the test-pollution guard the existing `gate-denial` kind already has
  (`friction-events.js`'s `parsed.test === true` skip) if this guard's own test suite exercises
  the same refusal path — otherwise this repo's own hook tests would inflate a real run's
  friction count.
- This record is scoped to observability only — the refusal mechanism's own correctness (whether
  it should refuse a given command at all) is #1798's territory, not this record's.

## Original request

**Summary:** The PreToolUse worktree-isolation guard refuses Bash commands it cannot prove are non-git (runtime-computed paths, heredocs mentioning commits, compound commands), but those refusals are not one of the five friction event kinds `bin/friction-events.js` returns, so `/claude-tweaks:reflect`'s Friction lens under-counts the single most frequent stop a worktree session experiences.
**Kind:** Gap
**Affected component:** `bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` (worktree-isolation guard) / `bin/friction-events.js` / `skills/reflect/full-mode.md` Friction lens
**Use case:**
Running `/claude-tweaks:flow` on a record inside a worktree (worktree-always: true), plugin 6.118.0. Over one build → test → review → wrap-up run, the guard refused roughly eight commands that were not version-control operations: `sed -n '...' "$R/decisions.md"` with `R` a shell variable holding the run-dir path, a `for` loop over `gh issue list --json` calls, and heredocs writing staged reflect files whose body text mentioned commit hashes. Each refusal was rewritten into a plain command with a literal path, or moved to the Write tool. At wrap-up, the Friction lens ran `friction-events.js --run <run-dir>` and saw 1 `bookkeeping-stamp-deny` and 13 `contract-violation` events, and zero `wd-deny`/`gate-denial` — the eight guard refusals left no trace, so the lens reported the run as proportionate when the operator's actual experience was dominated by them. The refusal itself is tracked in #1798; this report is about its observability.
**Definition:** Clear — log each guard refusal as a friction event (a new kind, e.g. `wd-guard-refusal`, carrying the refused command's executable and the refusal reason) and add it to `full-mode.md`'s friction-lens vocabulary block so the pinned vocabulary test covers it.
**Plugin version:** 6.118.0

groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

`review/code-mode-steps.md`'s Step 6.7 (Late Findings Routing) and `design-wrapper/modes/polish.md`'s Step 5 (suggestion-driven dispatch) both independently consume the same `source: "audit"` findings from the shared cache `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{feature}-audit.json` (`design-wrapper/modes/review.md`'s Step 5, the cache's sole producer) — Step 6.7 routes each finding by severity under the run's ceiling (low → AUTO, medium/high → STAGED, critical → KEPT-PROMPT), while polish's Step 5 independently applies whatever command each finding's own `suggestion` field names, with no awareness of what review already decided. When both run in the same `/claude-tweaks:flow` (review, then polish, per the pipeline order), polish's blind suggestion-driven dispatch can re-derive and auto-apply a finding review had just staged for a human — bypassing the ceiling entirely.

**Design resolved before shaping (the record's own two-option Open Question):** traced the actual cache mechanism directly. Both Step 6.7 and polish's Step 5 read the exact same JSON structure (`review.md` Step 5's documented cache shape: `{spec, written_at, findings: [{id, source, category, severity, message, suggestion}, ...]}`), and nothing currently writes back to it after review resolves a finding's routing — that's the actual gap, not a missing precedence rule. Option (a) — polish defers to review's routing via a disposition field on the cache entry — is directly buildable on this existing shared structure with no new plumbing. Option (b) — review leaves suggestion-bearing audit findings to polish entirely — is rejected: it would mean a **high-severity** audit finding carrying a `suggestion` never reaches Step 6.7's ceiling-aware human-staging at all, unconditionally auto-applied by polish regardless of severity — the opposite of what Step 6.7 exists to guarantee.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 2-3

## Non-Goals

- Any change to Step 6.7's own severity-routing rules (`step3-routing.md`'s AUTO/STAGED/KEPT-PROMPT thresholds) — this spec only adds a write-back of the *outcome*, not a change to how that outcome is decided.
- Any change to `craft-critic` or `critique` finding handling — the disposition field applies only to `source: "audit"` cache entries, the only kind polish's Step 5 three-way table dispatches by `suggestion` at all (`craft-critic` entries are Step 4's context, never Step 5's dispatch key, per `polish.md`'s own three-way consumption table).
- Cross-run or cross-invocation coordination — this only guards the in-flow ordering (review's Step 6.7, then polish's Step 5, within one `/claude-tweaks:flow` run) where both read the same cache file the same run produced.

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` (~line 373-390): Step 5, the cache's sole writer. Filters to `source === "audit" || (source === "craft-critic" && target === "code")`. Cache shape documented in full (see Overview above). "Primary path" (`docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{feature}-audit.json`) vs "Fallback" (`docs/plans/audit-{spec-slug}.json`) path resolution is stated once here — Step 6.7's write-back must resolve the same path the same way, not re-derive its own rule.
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7 (~line 293-306): routes "Design Quality" findings (populated from the wrapper's `review` mode output, which itself is audit + craft-critic-normalized-into-critique-shape per `code-mode-steps.md` ~line 277/289) via `step3-routing.md`'s severity rules. Currently reads the cached findings for display/routing only — never writes back to the cache file.
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` (~line 49-58): the three-way consumption table for `source: "audit"` cache entries — usable `suggestion` → Command (Step 5); `suggestion: null`/unresolvable → Staged observation (`kind: "unclassified"`); no third branch exists for "already routed by review."
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` Step 5 (~line 91-101): "Read the audit findings from Step 3 — the cache entries with `source: "audit"` only... Dispatch what the finding names." No check against any prior disposition.
- Ordering guarantee: `/claude-tweaks:flow` invokes `design-wrapper polish` mode "after review passes" (`design-wrapper/SKILL.md`'s "When to Use" list) — within one flow run, Step 6.7 always resolves before polish's Step 5 ever reads the cache, so a write-then-read ordering is safe by construction for the in-flow case this spec targets.
- Standalone `/claude-tweaks:design-wrapper polish` (outside a flow context, `docs/plans/audit-{spec-slug}.json`): review's Step 6.7 may never have run at all — no cache entry would carry a disposition field in that case, and polish's existing three-way table applies unchanged. This is a safe, natural degrade requiring no special-casing (Non-Goals above).

## Deliverables

- [ ] `review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7: after resolving each Design-Quality-category finding sourced from `audit` (not visual, not a craft-critic-only entry with no cache counterpart), write a `dispositionByReview: {status: "applied"|"staged"|"accepted"|"deferred"|"kept-prompt", at: "<ISO timestamp>"}` field onto that finding's entry in the same cache file `review.md` Step 5 wrote — an in-place read-modify-write (read the existing JSON, find the entry by `id`, set the field, write the whole file back) — never a blind overwrite that would drop other entries' existing fields. Resolve the cache file path the same way `review.md` Step 5 does (Primary/Fallback), not a new derivation.
- [ ] `design-wrapper/modes/polish.md`'s three-way consumption table (~line 49-58) gains a new first-checked branch: a `source: "audit"` entry that already carries a `dispositionByReview` field (any value) is **skipped entirely** — not dispatched as a Command, not staged as an unclassified observation. State this explicitly as a fourth row in the table, checked before the existing `suggestion`-based branches.
- [ ] `polish.md` Step 5's own prose (~line 93): add the skip check as the first step of the per-finding loop, before reading `suggestion`.
- [ ] State in both files' prose that this is what makes review's ceiling-aware routing authoritative over polish's blind suggestion-driven dispatch — the precedence the record's own use-case found undocumented.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After Step 6.7 resolves a `source: "audit"` finding's routing, the cache file's matching entry (by `id`) carries a `dispositionByReview` field with the resolved status — verified by a fixture cache file + a test asserting the field is present and correctly valued after a simulated Step 6.7 resolution for each of the four severity outcomes.
2. Every other field on that entry (`source`, `category`, `severity`, `message`, `suggestion`, and every other entry in `findings`) is unchanged by the write — verified by a test asserting only the targeted entry's `dispositionByReview` field differs from the pre-write cache.
3. `polish.md`'s Step 5, given a cache where one `source: "audit"` entry carries `dispositionByReview` and another does not, dispatches a command (or stages an unclassified observation) for the undisposed entry only — the disposed entry produces neither — verified by a fixture test.
4. A cache with no `dispositionByReview` field on any entry (the standalone-polish, review-never-ran case) behaves exactly as it does today — no regression to existing suggestion-driven dispatch tests.
5. `npm test` passes with no regressions.

## Technical Approach

Reuses the cache file both consumers already share rather than inventing new inter-skill plumbing (a lock file, an env var, a separate coordination artifact) — the fix is entirely a read-modify-write on data that already flows through both files. The skip check in `polish.md` is a presence check on the field (any value means "review already handled this"), not a value-based branch, since polish never needs to know *which* terminal status review chose — only that review already decided.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 6.7 (~line 293-306), the write-back
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` — Step 5 (~line 373-390), reference only for the cache shape/path-resolution rule Step 6.7's write must match
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` — the three-way consumption table (~line 49-58) and Step 5 (~line 91-101), the skip check
- Existing test coverage for `polish.md`'s suggestion-driven dispatch and `review`'s Step 6.7 (locate via `grep -rl "suggestion-driven\|Step 6.7\|dispositionByReview" tests/`) — extend with the new fixture cases

## Gotchas

- The write-back must be a read-modify-write against the existing cache file, never a fresh overwrite — `review.md` Step 5's own cache write already happened earlier in the same run (it's the producer), and Step 6.7's write is a later, additive update to the same file, not a second production pass.
- Scope the disposition field to `source: "audit"` entries only — `craft-critic` entries have no `suggestion`-driven dispatch path in polish's Step 5 to guard against (they're Step 4's context, consumed differently), so writing a disposition onto them would be inert but also potentially confusing; don't do it.
- The ordering guarantee (review's Step 6.7 before polish's Step 5, within one flow run) is what makes this fix sufficient — this spec does not need to solve for review and polish running concurrently or out of order, which the current pipeline structure doesn't produce.

## Original request

**Summary:** An Impeccable `audit` finding can be staged for a human by review Step 6.7 and, minutes later, auto-applied by `design-wrapper polish`'s suggestion-driven dispatch of the same finding's `suggestion` — the two files never say which route wins.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** skills/review/code-mode-steps.md (Step 6.7 Late Findings Routing) and skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md (Step 5 suggestion-driven dispatch)

**Use case:** In a `/claude-tweaks:flow` run, `audit` reported two accessibility findings on a form (a missing `aria-describedby`; two show/hide toggles sharing one accessible name), each carrying `suggestion: harden`. Review Step 6.7 routed them by severity under the run's ceiling — one staged for the Review Console (high), one auto-applied (medium). The flow's polish phase then ran `design-wrapper polish`, whose Step 5 dispatches the `harden` command each cached finding's `suggestion` names — which would re-derive and apply the very finding review had just staged for a human, bypassing the ceiling. The executing agent noticed and had polish honour review's routing (logged as a KEPT-PROMPT-shaped anomaly note), but nothing in either file states the precedence, so the next run may resolve it the other way.

Two viable fixes, no preference stated here: (a) polish's suggestion-driven dispatch skips any cached audit finding review Step 6.7 already routed — the cache entry could carry review's disposition (`applied` / `staged`) and polish dispatches only unrouted ones; or (b) Step 6.7 leaves audit findings that carry a usable `suggestion` to polish and routes only critique/critic findings.

**Definition:** Needed — two directions ((a) polish defers to review's routing via a disposition field on the cache entry; (b) review leaves suggestion-bearing audit findings to polish) with no tradeoff made yet.

**Plugin version:** 6.118.0
